title.zh: GCM 伽罗瓦计数器模式

entries.relatedPolicy: Related entries are distinct concepts; no merge or replacement is implied.

zh.principle: **算法**：GCM 伽罗瓦计数器模式（Galois/Counter Mode）。两条职责分工由同一份建议书写明：「GCM provides assurance of the confidentiality of data using a variation of the Counter mode of operation for encryption.」机密性走计数器模式的变体；紧随其后的句子把真实性交给定义在二元伽罗瓦域（即有限域）上的通用杂凑函数，并说这份真实性覆盖密文数据每次调用不超过约 64 吉字节——注意这个上限挂在真实性保障上，同一节随后另说，不必加密的附加数据可「of practically unlimited length per invocation」。该条目只写这份文档说到的部分：它没有给 GHASH 的乘法定义，也没有把密钥调度算作 GCM 的一部分。
zh.why: 为什么要用代数结构做认证而不是校验和：文档给的理由是「GCM provides stronger authentication assurance than a (non-cryptographic) checksum or error detecting code」，并把它分成两层——既能发现偶然的改动，也能发现恶意改动；同一段还说，输入若限定在不需要机密性的材料上，本模式就成了文档所称的 GMAC，此时它不过是对该输入的一种认证模式。也就是说，这里买到的不是更快的校验和，而是在密钥之下对伪造的抵抗。
zh.used: 用途与位置先由文档自陈：「Thus, GCM is a mode of operation of the AES algorithm.」它是 AES 的一个工作模式，而不是独立密码；同一节还声明关于 GCM 的论断同样适用于 GMAC，所以关于本模式的说法一并覆盖只做认证的那个特化。发布身份同样可查：第 2 节写着「This Recommendation has been prepared for use by federal agencies.」，紧接的一句补充非政府组织可自愿使用——前者是应用标签里 government 的依据，后者不构成行业用途的证据。基础设施那一标签只有编辑性支撑：本库应用轴词汇里可能用来打标的协议名一个都没出现——IPsec、TLS、802.11 各 grep 0 次——但文档确实在别处点了协议名，具体例子有两个——第 5.2.1.1 节网络协议里的 AAD 字段，以及附录 C 点名的「Secure Real-time Transport Protocol carrying Voice over Internet Protocol, running over User Datagram Protocol」。
zh.broken: 限度不在算法强度上，而在使用条件上：文档给出的警告是「a breach of the requirement in Sec.8 for the uniqueness of the initialization strings may compromise the security assurance almost entirely」，并据此要求无法确保唯一性时就不要上这个模式。第 5.2.1.1 节把 IV 说成本质上是一次性数，即在指定上下文内取唯一值的量。第 8.3 节给同一把密钥的总调用次数设上限，但那是有条件的：它适用于采用「the deterministic construction with IVs whose length is not 96」或 RBG-based construction 的一切实现，只对只用 96 位确定性 IV 的实现例外。本副本把该全局上限印成 232，出版物在那里排的是上标，亦即 2 的 32 次方；同一小节接着用一支 210 台的示例设备群把这个全局数字拆成每台设备的局部限额，示例数同样丢了指数。这些数字在本副本里无一可原样引用，所以该条目只述这个约束的形状，不复述其数字。

en.principle: **Algorithm**: Galois/Counter Mode (GCM 伽罗瓦计数器模式). The division of labour is stated by the recommendation itself: "GCM provides assurance of the confidentiality of data using a variation of the Counter mode of operation for encryption." Confidentiality comes from a variation of counter mode, and the sentence that follows hands authenticity to a universal hash function over a binary Galois field - finite, in the document's parenthesis. Its parenthesis caps that authenticity assurance at about 64 gigabytes of confidential data per invocation - the limit sits on the authenticity of the encrypted part, and the same section says separately that additional data needing no encryption may be "of practically unlimited length per invocation". This entry stays inside what that document says: it does not reproduce the multiplication that defines GHASH, and it does not treat the key schedule as part of GCM.
en.why: Why authentication is built on algebra rather than on a checksum: the document's stated reason is that "GCM provides stronger authentication assurance than a (non-cryptographic) checksum or error detecting code", and it splits the point into two cases - accidental modification and deliberate modification. The same passage adds that an input confined to material needing no confidentiality turns the mode into what the document calls GMAC, which is then nothing more than an authentication mode over that input. What is bought here is therefore resistance to forgery under a key, not a faster checksum.
en.used: The position comes from the document's own words: "Thus, GCM is a mode of operation of the AES algorithm." It is a mode of AES rather than a stand-alone cipher, and the same section states that everything said about GCM also applies to GMAC, so claims about the mode cover the authentication-only specialization as well. Its standing is equally checkable: Section 2 prints "This Recommendation has been prepared for use by federal agencies.", and the next sentence adds that nongovernmental organizations may use it voluntarily - the first is what the government application label rests on, the second is not evidence of any industry use. The infrastructure label has only editorial support. None of the protocol names this KB's application vocabulary might have been labelled from occurs - IPsec, TLS and 802.11 each grep to zero - but the document does name protocols elsewhere: its two concrete examples are the network-protocol AAD fields in Sec. 5.2.1.1 and, in Appendix C, "Secure Real-time Transport Protocol carrying Voice over Internet Protocol, running over User Datagram Protocol". A draft of this entry said no protocol name occurs anywhere; that was refuted by line 1439 and is corrected here.
en.broken: The limit is a condition of use rather than a strength result: the document warns that "a breach of the requirement in Sec. 8 for the uniqueness of the initialization strings may compromise the security assurance almost entirely", and it concludes that the mode stays undeployed where that uniqueness cannot be ensured. Sec. 5.2.1.1 describes the IV as essentially a nonce - unique inside the context that the document specifies. Sec. 8.3 caps how many times one key may be used at all, and the cap is conditional: it applies to every implementation using either "the deterministic construction with IVs whose length is not 96" or the RBG-based construction, and it is waived only where 96-bit IVs from the deterministic construction are the sole case. This copy prints that global ceiling as 232 where the publication sets a superscript, i.e. two to the thirty-second, and the same subsection then splits it into per-device limits through an example fleet of 210 units, likewise printed without its exponent. Every one of those digits is damaged in this extraction, so this entry states the shape of the constraint and does not quote the numbers.
en.history: The names come from this file itself: "The designers of GCM are McGrew and Viega." The same sentence logs the NIST submission as Ref. [6] and the security-and-performance discussion as Ref. [7], and its bibliography dates those two: [6] is "The Galois/Counter Mode of Operation (GCM)", May 31, 2005, and [7] is "The Security and Performance of the Galois/Counter Mode (GCM) of Operation", INDOCRYPT '04, 2004. Neither is the 《GCM and GMAC》(2007) record the row inherited, and no copy of either paper is retained here, so what is verifiable is this recommendation's own report of it - the acknowledgements separately print "David McGrew, who co-invented GCM and submitted it to NIST". Three printed dates carry the dating: the title page on line 2 sets "November, 2007" with a comma, line 23 sets November 2007 on the title page and line 51 is the running imprint, which also gives the 37-page extent. So the row's era moves from e14-standardization, whose era.md prints a 1977-2001 window that excludes 2007, to e15-web-protocols, which prints 1991-2010. No document retained here gives the year McGrew and Viega proposed the mode, so none is added.

zh: GCM：把计数器模式的加密与伽罗瓦域上的认证结合起来的分组密码工作模式。
GMAC：当输入只作认证、不作加密时，GCM 的特化形式；文中声明关于 GCM 的论断同样适用于它。
GHASH：在二元伽罗瓦域上定义、用于认证部分的通用杂凑函数。
初始化向量 IV：本质上是一次性数，即在指定上下文内取唯一值。
附加数据 AAD：参与认证但不必加密的那部分数据。
唯一性要求：第 8 节把它写成一个概率上限——同一 IV 与同一密钥再次相遇的概率不得大于给定界，出版物该处排上标，本副本印成 2-32。
en: GCM: a block cipher mode that combines counter-mode encryption with authentication over a Galois field.
GMAC: the specialization of GCM to data that is only authenticated; the document extends its statements about GCM to this case as well.
GHASH: the universal hash function, defined over a binary Galois field, that carries the authentication part.
initialization vector (IV): the document calls it essentially a nonce - one quantity, used once, inside the context it is defined for.
additional authenticated data (AAD): data that is authenticated without necessarily being confidential.

uniqueness requirement: Sec. 8 states it as a probability ceiling - the chance of ever pairing one IV with one key twice must stay no greater than a bound the document prints with a superscript, which this extraction renders as 2-32.
